name: Golda Meir
role: Prime Minister of Israel (1969-1974); foreign minister 1956-1966
summary: A Labor Zionist who held that the Jews need a sovereign state and defended Israel's security above territorial compromise, refusing to divide Jerusalem and denying a separate Palestinian state west of the Jordan. She called herself a socialist in the Swedish, freedom-respecting sense, opposed colonialism and apartheid, and backed disarmament and aid for developing countries.

arms-reduction.rationale: In UN speeches from 1957 to 1965 she called for general disarmament with mutual inspection, saying armaments drain resources and disarmament would be an unqualified blessing.

civil-marriage.rationale: JTA reported she ruled out civil marriage for Israel as divisive, and threatened to resign with her Cabinet if a coalition partner backed a limited civil marriage bill in 1972.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: She called murders of unarmed civilians by fedayeen 'wanton and indiscriminate' at the UN, and told Fallaci that attacks on school buses and supermarkets were infamy, even opposing the Irgun and Stern on this ground.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: At the UN in 1963 and 1965 she said Israel opposed colonialism wherever it exists and supported the liberation of every African territory still under colonial rule.

democratic-peace.rationale: She told Fallaci peace with the Arab states would come only through their evolution toward democracy, since a dictator need not answer to his people for a peace he does not make.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: She told Fallaci that Jews had come to Israel from all over the world 'as we wanted', and at the UN described Israel absorbing Jewish refugees from Europe and Arab lands as its mission.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: At the UN in 1963 she said all men are created equal and that Israel abhors discrimination on grounds of race, colour or religion.

holocaust-denial.rationale: At the UN in 1956 she stated that six million of Europe's Jews were slaughtered by the Nazis and referred to the crematoria and the extermination of a people.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: She describes Zionism's aim as gathering the Jews of the world into Israel (the ingathering), not as supporting diaspora culture in preference to that.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: At the UN in 1956 she called the 1947 resolution creating a Jewish state the basis of Israel, and told Fallaci that seeing justice for the Jewish people through a sovereign state was the purpose of her life.

military-superiority.rationale: In her March 1974 Knesset statement she said Israel must keep building the IDF so it can win decisively, and that its superiority had been proved in the war.

national-self-determination.rationale: She backed national independence for African territories at the UN in 1965 but told Fallaci there must be no third Arab state between Israel and Jordan and denied a distinct Palestinian people.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: She told Fallaci Jerusalem, the Golan and Gaza would never be given up, but also that Israel would give back most of Sinai and probably part of the West Bank in a peace; the same interview points both ways.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: She told Fallaci that men never obstructed her career and she had no inferiority complex, but also that women must be far more capable to succeed and that injustices persist on party lists.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: She told Fallaci that terror groups are not a revolutionary movement and that she always opposed the Irgun and Stern groups of the Mandate period, while defending state military force.

promote-ethnic-return-migration.rationale: Her UN speeches present the ingathering of Jewish refugees and immigrants as Israel's historic mission, and she told Fallaci the point was bringing Jews in from everywhere.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: At the UN in 1956 she appealed to Egypt to stop persecuting its Jewish population and told Fallaci of Jews persecuted in Russia, speaking for Jews outside Israel.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: At the UN in 1963 she condemned apartheid and said Israel opposes racial discrimination wherever it exists.

refugee-return.rationale: Asked by Fallaci whether Palestinian refugees could return, she said 'Impossible' and that they could not come back among Israelis; she held the Arab states responsible for resettling them.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: At the UN in 1965 she said advanced countries must not prosper through terms of trade that keep poorer countries poor and dependent on aid.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: At the UN in 1960 she endorsed a proposal that industrial nations divert 2 per cent of their gross product to developing countries, and in 1962 urged easier-term capital for them.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: At the UN in 1956 she rejected the charge that Israel is an instrument of colonialism; she did not address settler states in general.

women-suffrage.rationale: She told Fallaci it was ridiculous that women still met reservations in politics and said women can be good heads of government.

notes: Themes searched: Zionism and territory, refugees, terrorism, disarmament, colonialism and race, development aid, socialism, women, religion and state. Domestic economy, government structure and civil liberties found no stated position in the sources reachable (her memoir was borrow-only). Her words and reported acts agree where both exist.
